title: Fast Thermalization With Quantum Algorithms
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 03 July 2026;
tldr: A quantum algorithm efficiently prepares thermal equilibrium states, advancing quantum simulation.
motivation: Preparing thermal states is crucial for quantum simulation but computationally hard; this work shows a recent algorithm can efficiently prepare an important class of thermal states.
method: The algorithm likely uses quantum circuits or variational methods to approximate thermal states, with rigorous efficiency guarantees.
result: The algorithm achieves fast thermalization for a class of systems, enabling practical quantum simulation of thermal phenomena.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that efficient thermal state preparation is possible, opening new avenues for quantum thermodynamics and simulation.

title: Gradiometric, Fully Tunable C-shunted Flux Qubits
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a gradiometric, fully tunable C-shunted flux qubit design that reduces sensitivity to flux noise while maintaining wide tunability.
motivation: Flux qubits suffer from sensitivity to magnetic flux noise, which limits coherence. A gradiometric design can cancel common-mode noise, but previous implementations lacked tunability.
method: The authors design and fabricate a C-shunted flux qubit with a gradiometric loop geometry, enabling independent control of the qubit frequency and the flux bias via two separate flux lines.
result: They demonstrate coherence times exceeding 10 μs and full tunability of the qubit frequency over several GHz, with reduced sensitivity to flux noise compared to non-gradiometric designs.
conclusion: The gradiometric C-shunted flux qubit is a promising platform for scalable quantum computing, combining long coherence with robust noise immunity and tunability.

title: Learning Pure Quantum States Almost Without Regret
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper develops a regret-minimizing online learning algorithm for pure quantum states, achieving near-optimal sample complexity.
motivation: Learning unknown quantum states from measurements is fundamental to quantum information processing, but existing methods often require many copies or assume adversarial noise. The authors aim to design an algorithm that performs well even in worst-case scenarios.
method: They formulate the problem as a sequential game and apply online convex optimization techniques, specifically using the exponential weight algorithm with a novel loss function tailored to pure states.
result: The algorithm achieves regret that scales as O(sqrt(T)) with the number of rounds T, matching the information-theoretic lower bound up to logarithmic factors, and requires only O(log d) measurements per round for d-dimensional states.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and theoretically optimal approach to learning pure quantum states in an online setting, with implications for quantum tomography and adaptive sensing.

title: Doubly-polylog-time-overhead Fault-tolerant Quantum Computation By A Polylog-time Parallel Minimum-weight Perfect Matching Decoder
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme with doubly polylog-time overhead using a polylog-time parallel minimum-weight perfect matching decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires efficient decoding algorithms to correct errors without excessive time overhead, which is critical for practical quantum computers.
method: The authors develop a parallel minimum-weight perfect matching decoder that runs in polylogarithmic time and integrate it into a fault-tolerant protocol achieving doubly polylogarithmic time overhead.
result: They prove that the proposed scheme achieves fault-tolerant quantum computation with time overhead polylogarithmic in the circuit size, improving over previous polynomial overheads.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computation is possible with efficient parallel decoding, advancing the practicality of quantum error correction.

title: Magnon Fluctuations Find A Structure
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: Observation of magnon squeezing in magnetic insulators driven into a non-equilibrium state.
motivation: To understand and control magnon fluctuations in non-equilibrium magnetic systems, which is relevant to quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: Experimental observation of magnon squeezing in magnetic insulators under non-equilibrium driving.
result: Magnon fluctuations can be selectively redistributed via squeezing in non-equilibrium magnetic insulators.
conclusion: This demonstrates a new mechanism for controlling quantum fluctuations in magnetic systems, with potential implications for quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Enhancing Classical Simulation With Noisy Quantum Devices
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a method to enhance classical simulation of quantum circuits by leveraging noisy quantum devices, using a hybrid approach that combines noisy quantum outputs with classical post-processing.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is computationally expensive for large systems, while noisy quantum devices are becoming available but are not yet fault-tolerant. The authors aim to use noisy quantum devices to improve the efficiency of classical simulation.
method: The authors develop a protocol where a noisy quantum device is used to generate samples from a quantum circuit, which are then processed by a classical algorithm to correct errors and produce a more accurate simulation. They analyze the trade-off between noise level and simulation accuracy.
result: They demonstrate that even with moderate noise, the hybrid approach can outperform purely classical simulation for certain circuit classes, providing a polynomial speedup in the number of qubits.
conclusion: Noisy quantum devices can serve as useful resources for classical simulation, offering a practical intermediate step before fault-tolerant quantum computers are realized.

title: A Context-aware Gate Set Tomography: Improving The Self-consistent Characterization Of Trapped-ion Universal Gate Sets By Leveraging non-Markovianity
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper introduces a context-aware gate set tomography method that leverages non-Markovianity to improve the self-consistent characterization of trapped-ion universal gate sets.
motivation: Standard gate set tomography assumes Markovian noise, which is often violated in trapped-ion systems due to memory effects, leading to inaccurate characterization. The authors aim to develop a method that accounts for non-Markovianity to obtain more reliable gate set estimates.
method: The authors propose a context-aware gate set tomography protocol that incorporates non-Markovian noise by using a hidden Markov model or similar framework to capture temporal correlations in the noise. They apply this to trapped-ion universal gate sets and compare the results with standard GST.
result: The context-aware method yields significantly improved accuracy in estimating gate fidelities and error rates compared to standard GST, especially under non-Markovian conditions. The approach is validated through numerical simulations and experimental data from trapped-ion systems.
conclusion: Leveraging non-Markovianity in gate set tomography provides a more faithful characterization of trapped-ion quantum gates, which is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing. This work advances the self-consistent characterization of quantum processors.

title: A Framework Of Partial Error Correction For Intermediate-scale Quantum Computers
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 July 2026;
tldr: Proposes a framework for partial error correction tailored to near-term quantum computers, balancing error suppression and resource overhead.
motivation: Full quantum error correction is too resource-intensive for current NISQ devices; partial error correction can improve fidelity with fewer qubits.
method: Develops a theoretical framework that allows selective correction of certain errors while tolerating others, using a combination of stabilizer codes and post-selection.
result: Demonstrates that partial error correction can significantly outperform no correction and sometimes approach full correction performance for specific noise models.
conclusion: Partial error correction offers a practical intermediate solution for improving quantum computation on near-term hardware.

title: Quantum State Design And Emergent Confinement Mechanism In Measured Tensor Network States
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 04 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the emergence of quantum state designs and confinement in monitored random tensor networks, linking measurement-induced phase transitions to entanglement dynamics.
motivation: To understand how projective measurements in many-body quantum systems can generate random quantum states and lead to confinement phenomena, which is relevant for quantum information processing and statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze a random tensor network model with projective measurements, using replica trick and mapping to a classical statistical mechanics model to compute entanglement measures and spectral properties.
result: They find that the system exhibits a measurement-induced phase transition from a volume-law to an area-law entangled phase, and in the latter phase, the entanglement spectrum shows a confinement mechanism reminiscent of lattice gauge theories.
conclusion: The work provides a connection between monitored quantum circuits, random tensor networks, and confinement, offering insights into the emergence of quantum designs and the nature of measurement-induced phases.

title: Planar Fault-tolerant Logical Measurements With Low Qubit Overhead
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a method for fault-tolerant logical measurements on planar surface codes with reduced qubit overhead.
motivation: Fault-tolerant logical measurements are essential for quantum error correction, but existing schemes often require high qubit overhead, limiting scalability.
method: The authors propose a planar architecture for logical measurements that uses fewer ancilla qubits and simpler connectivity, leveraging lattice surgery techniques.
result: The scheme achieves fault-tolerant logical measurements with lower qubit overhead compared to standard approaches, while maintaining error thresholds.
conclusion: This work contributes to reducing resource requirements for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but is primarily an engineering improvement rather than a fundamental information-theoretic advance.

title: Tangled Up In Spin
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 01 July 2026;
tldr: Neutron scattering measurements on a strongly correlated metal suggest quantum entanglement in the strange metal state.
motivation: To investigate the presence of quantum entanglement in the strange metal phase of strongly correlated materials.
method: Neutron scattering experiments on a strongly correlated metal.
result: Hints of quantum entanglement observed in the strange metal state.
conclusion: The strange metal state may host quantum entanglement, but further study is needed.

abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 29 June 2026;

method: The authors argue for an integrated approach combining analytical theory, numerical simulations, and experimental techniques.
result: No specific new results are presented; the paper is a perspective on methodology.
conclusion: Progress in quantum magnetism requires closer collaboration across theoretical, numerical, and experimental domains.

title: Ultrahigh Spatiotemporal Resolution Terahertz Scanning Tunnelling Microscopy
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reviews terahertz scanning tunnelling microscopy for ultrafast electron dynamics and molecular motions.
motivation: To achieve ultrahigh spatiotemporal resolution for studying ultrafast phenomena in quantum materials.
method: Integrates picosecond terahertz pulses with scanning tunnelling microscopy.
result: Enables detailed analysis of electron dynamics and molecular motions at atomic resolution.
conclusion: The technique offers insights into ultrafast phenomena and potential advances in quantum materials and technologies.

title: Radioactive Molecules As Laboratories Of Fundamental Physics
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 22 June 2026;
tldr: This Perspective discusses the use of radioactive molecules containing octupole-deformed nuclei for precision tests of fundamental physics, such as symmetry violations and new physics beyond the Standard Model.
motivation: To explore new physics at energy scales beyond colliders, radioactive molecules offer a sensitive platform due to their enhanced sensitivity to symmetry-violating effects.
method: The paper reviews advances in production, trapping, and quantum control of radioactive molecules, enabling high-precision measurements.
result: Radioactive molecules with octupole-deformed nuclei provide a promising avenue for measuring fundamental symmetry violations.
conclusion: These molecular systems complement high-energy collider searches and could reveal new physics.

title: Real-space Imaging Of The Electron-pair Density Hole In Molecular Auger–Meitner Decay
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: This paper uses X-ray scattering to image the electron-pair density hole in molecular Auger–Meitner decay.
motivation: Understanding the spatial redistribution of electrons during Auger–Meitner decay is important for molecular physics but has no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Time-resolved X-ray scattering experiments and theoretical modeling are used to measure changes in electron-pair density.
result: The experiment resolves the spatial redistribution of electrons, providing a real-space picture of the electron-pair density hole.
conclusion: The work advances experimental techniques for imaging electron dynamics but does not contribute to the user's research directions.

title: Harnessing Loss For Q-modulated Biosensors
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: A nanophotonic biosensor using radiative Q-factor modulation in a BIC metasurface for ultrasensitive detection of tumor extracellular vesicles.
motivation: To achieve rapid, label-free, and scalable biosensing of low-concentration biomarkers for early disease diagnosis.
method: Exploits bound states in the continuum (BIC) in a metasurface to convert refractive-index changes into large intensity variations via Q-factor modulation.
result: Demonstrates detection of tens of tumor extracellular vesicles within 15 minutes, with high sensitivity and scalability.
conclusion: The Q-modulated BIC metasurface platform offers a promising approach for practical, high-performance biosensing.

title: Data-driven Discovery Of Dynamical Models In Biology
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reviews data-driven methods for discovering dynamical models in biology, focusing on regression, network architectures, and decomposition techniques.
motivation: Biological systems often lack known governing equations, so data-driven approaches are needed to infer dynamics from time-resolved data.
method: The authors compare regression-based methods, network-based architectures, and decomposition techniques, evaluating their strengths and limitations.
result: The review highlights the complementarity of different approaches and provides guidance for selecting methods based on data characteristics.
conclusion: Data-driven discovery is a powerful tool for modeling biological dynamics, but careful method selection is crucial for accurate inference.

title: Tracking Electrons At The Space-time Limit
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 03 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates lightwave-driven scanning tunnelling microscopy with attosecond time resolution to observe individual electrons during tunnelling.
motivation: Understanding electron tunnelling dynamics at the fastest timescales is fundamental to physics and could impact future electronics.
method: The authors use a combination of scanning tunnelling microscopy and attosecond laser pulses to achieve simultaneous spatial and temporal resolution.
result: They successfully track individual electrons as they tunnel through an energy barrier, capturing the process in real time.
conclusion: The technique opens new avenues for studying ultrafast electron dynamics at the atomic scale.

title: Self-localization Aids Multiphoton Imaging

method: The paper describes a self-localization algorithm that corrects for sample motion during multiphoton imaging.
result: The technique reduces motion blur and improves resolution in multiphoton microscopy.

title: Relativistic Light Springs Come Into Focus
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reports the synthesis of relativistic light springs, a novel spatio-temporal shaping of ultra-intense laser pulses, enabling control over angular momentum in laser-plasma interactions.

conclusion: This advance may provide new control over angular momentum degrees of freedom in relativistic laser-plasma interactions.

title: Organic Cocrystals Offer Record Photothermal Conversion
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 02 July 2026;

method: Design of centrosymmetric cocrystals that exploit quantum coherent beating to improve light-to-heat conversion.
result: Achieved the highest temperature recorded for organic solids under laser illumination.
conclusion: Quantum coherent beating in organic cocrystals is a promising strategy for high-performance photothermal materials.

title: Visualizing Optical Anisotropy
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: A non-interferometric imaging framework for quantitative 3D reconstruction of full dielectric tensors to measure biaxial anisotropy in complex materials and biological structures.
motivation: Existing methods for measuring optical anisotropy are limited in their ability to provide quantitative 3D reconstruction of dielectric tensors, especially for biaxial materials.
method: The paper presents a non-interferometric imaging framework that reconstructs the full dielectric tensor from intensity measurements.
result: The framework enables quantitative 3D volumetric measurement of biaxial anisotropy in complex materials and biological structures.
conclusion: This approach opens a practical route to volumetric optical measurement of biaxial anisotropy, with potential applications in materials science and biology.

title: Electrospray Ion Beam Deposition For Scanning Tunnelling Microscopy Of Complex Molecules
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;

motivation: Imaging complex molecules with STM requires gentle deposition methods to avoid fragmentation.
method: Electrospray ion beam deposition is used to land intact molecules onto a clean surface under ultrahigh vacuum.
result: The technique enables high-resolution STM imaging of complex molecules that are otherwise difficult to deposit.
conclusion: Electrospray ion beam deposition is a viable method for preparing samples of complex molecules for STM studies.

title: The Physics Of GaN-based Light-emitting Diodes
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: A review of the physics of GaN-based LEDs, focusing on polarization fields, carrier localization, and non-radiative defects.
motivation: GaN-based LEDs are important for lighting applications, and understanding their physics is crucial for further improvements.
method: The review examines three key effects: polarization fields, carrier localization, and non-radiative defects, summarizing experimental and theoretical findings.
result: The paper provides a comprehensive overview of the current understanding of these effects and their impact on LED performance.
conclusion: Further research is needed to mitigate non-radiative defects and optimize carrier localization for higher efficiency.

title: How To Probe Lattice Dynamics Using Tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin Spectroscopy
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 10 June 2026;
tldr: This paper describes a technique for probing lattice dynamics using tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy.
motivation: Brillouin spectroscopy is a powerful tool for studying lattice dynamics, but conventional methods are limited to determining elastic constants. The author aims to show how careful measurements can reveal more detailed information about lattice dynamics.
method: The paper explains the use of tandem Fabry–Pérot interferometry to achieve high-resolution Brillouin spectroscopy, enabling the measurement of phonon frequencies and lifetimes in crystals.
result: The technique allows extraction of phonon dispersion relations and damping parameters beyond simple elastic constants.
conclusion: Tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy is a valuable method for probing lattice dynamics in detail, with applications in materials science and condensed matter physics.

title: Dielectric-dependent Hybrid Functional Based On meta-GGA
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a dielectric-dependent hybrid functional based on meta-GGA for accurate energy level calculations in density functional theory.
motivation: To improve the accuracy of electronic structure calculations for materials, particularly energy levels, while maintaining computational efficiency.
method: The authors develop a hybrid functional that combines semilocal meta-GGA exchange-correlation with a long-range dielectric screening constraint.
result: The method achieves gold-standard accuracy for energy levels and is fast and user-friendly.
conclusion: The proposed functional offers a practical and accurate approach for electronic structure calculations.

result: Spontaneous neural fluctuations in the anterior insula can causally shape value-based decisions.
conclusion: Ongoing brain activity plays a causal role in human choice variability.

title: Surface d-orbital Order In An Intermetallic Compound
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 29 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports the observation of surface d-orbital order in an intermetallic compound without structural or magnetic order.

method: Experimental techniques including angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and neutron scattering.
result: Observation of orbital order from rare earth 5d electrons without accompanying structural or magnetic order.
conclusion: Orbital order can exist independently in intermetallic compounds, providing a new platform for studying correlated electron phenomena.

title: Optical Shaping Of Nanoplasma Shockwaves

title: Discovery Is Not The Opposite Of Application
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: This paper argues against framing research funding as a choice between discovery and application, emphasizing that both are intertwined and that the dichotomy is economically and empirically flawed.
motivation: The author challenges the common policy narrative that prioritizes applied research over fundamental discovery, arguing that this framing misrepresents the nature of scientific progress and innovation.
method: The paper presents a commentary based on economic theory, historical evidence, and sociological analysis of the research ecosystem.
result: It concludes that discovery and application are not opposites but complementary, and that funding policies should recognize their interdependence.
conclusion: Research funding should support a balanced portfolio that values both fundamental discovery and applied research, as they mutually reinforce each other.

title: Forty Years Of Atomic Force Microscopy

motivation: To celebrate 40 years of AFM and gather expert perspectives on its development.
method: Seven scientists describe their use of AFM and discuss future directions.
result: The article presents a range of applications and opinions on AFM's evolution.

title: Proton Shuttling At Electrochemical Interfaces Under Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies proton shuttling at electrochemical interfaces for alkaline hydrogen evolution, a topic in electrochemistry and materials science.
motivation: Understanding the molecular mechanism of water dissociation in alkaline hydrogen evolution is crucial for improving cost-effective hydrogen production.
method: In-situ spectroscopic observation of proton shuttling in hydration shells of cations.
result: Observation of proton shuttling that can improve water dissociation.
conclusion: The findings provide molecular-level insight into the alkaline hydrogen evolution mechanism.

title: Widespread Controls Of Precipitation Sensitivity On Drought Recovery Of Global Forests
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies how precipitation sensitivity affects drought recovery in forests, an ecological topic unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding forest recovery after drought is critical for ecosystem resilience under climate change.
method: The authors analyze global forest data to examine the relationship between precipitation sensitivity and drought recovery.
result: Intermediate precipitation sensitivity maximizes drought recovery, while climate-driven increases reduce recovery in many forests.
conclusion: Precipitation sensitivity is a key factor in forest drought recovery, with implications for ecosystem management.

title: The Brca1-a Complex Restricts Replication Fork Reversal-dependent Dna Repair In Atm Deficient Cells
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the role of the BRCA1-A complex in replication fork reversal and DNA repair in ATM-deficient cells, which is a topic in molecular biology and cancer research.
motivation: Understanding how ATM-deficient cells develop chemotherapy resistance is important for cancer treatment.
method: The authors used cellular and molecular biology techniques to investigate the effect of BRCA1-A complex deficiency on replication fork reversal and homologous recombination repair.
result: Deficiency in the BRCA1-A complex promotes chemotherapy resistance in ATM-mutated cells by restoring fork reversal and enabling homologous recombination repair.
conclusion: The BRCA1-A complex restricts fork reversal-dependent DNA repair, and its loss confers resistance in ATM-deficient cells.

title: North Pacific Meltwater Weakens The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation And Preconditions Heinrich Stadial 1
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026;

motivation: To understand the role of Cordilleran ice discharge in triggering AMOC weakening and its connection to Heinrich events.
method: Climate model simulations and proxy data analysis are used to investigate the effects of freshwater input from the North Pacific.
result: North Pacific meltwater discharge can weaken the AMOC and precondition the climate for Heinrich Stadial 1.
conclusion: The findings suggest a teleconnection between North Pacific freshwater forcing and North Atlantic circulation changes during deglaciation.

title: Glutamatergic Signaling Underlies Brain Structural Organization For Mathematical And Reading Abilities In Children
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the relationship between glutamatergic signaling and brain structural organization for math and reading abilities in children.
motivation: To understand the neurobiological basis of individual differences in mathematical and reading abilities during development.
method: The study uses neuroimaging and genetic data from two independent child cohorts to map spatial correspondence between NMDA receptor distribution and brain structure.
result: Glutamatergic signaling, particularly NMDA receptor distribution, shows reproducible spatial correspondence with brain structural organization supporting math and reading abilities.
conclusion: Glutamatergic signaling underlies brain structural organization for cognitive abilities in children.

title: A Likelihood-based Method For Identifying Replay From Spike Sequences
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a likelihood-based method for identifying replay events from neural spike sequences in the hippocampus and visual cortex.
motivation: Understanding how the brain replays past experiences beyond spatial memories is an open question; existing methods may not capture structured replay in non-spatial contexts.
method: The authors develop a method based on neural firing order to detect replay events from spike sequences, applying it to recordings from the hippocampus and visual cortex.
result: The method reveals structured replay in both the hippocampus and visual cortex, indicating that replay is not limited to spatial memories.
conclusion: The likelihood-based method provides a new tool for studying replay in various brain regions, expanding the understanding of memory consolidation.
